messages:
Alex (Eng): Thanks for the security deep-dive today. Quick follow-up I forgot to ask during the Q&A — for Private deployments, what's the recommended audit log retention and is exporting logs to customer SIEM supported? I have a customer asking for 7+ years.

Maria (Security): Short answer: configurable per deployment. Defaults: hosted API = 90 days, Dedicated = 1 year. Private can be configured longer (we've done multi-year retention for enterprise customers) but it depends on contract + storage sizing. Exports are supported (S3-compatible export, syslog/Graylog over VPC). I'll post a doc link later. :link:

Jordan (Product): Adding a product note: export options are under Console > Settings > Logs for Dedicated/Private. For Private there is an "external-export" toggle. Be aware of egress/transfer cost implications if exporting to customer account. For long retention we recommend lifecycle policies + compression/encryption-at-rest.

Emily (Privacy): Heads up: retention >1 year can trigger additional privacy/regulatory reviews in some regions (e.g., CN/EU). If you have a specific customer/location, ping me and I'll validate DSAR/retention constraints. Archives may need redaction workflows.

Sam (SRE): Technical detail: audit logs are write-once append-only and signed at ingestion. We HMAC-sign batches and keep chain integrity metadata. Key rotation for signing is monthly by default. If customers require BYOK for signing key we can support a customer-managed HSM in Private deployments.

Alex (Eng): BYOK for signing — does that mean customer provides the HSM keys and Redwood never sees the plaintext key material?

Maria (Security): Correct. BYOK/HSM model: customer supplies KMS/HSM endpoint or we integrate with their KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSM). We store only key references/GRANTS, not key material. For AWS we use a Grant model; for on-prem HSM we talk over mTLS to their HSM proxy and call sign APIs. We'll add an architecture diagram to docs. :white_check_mark:

Jordan (Product): Roadmap note: Q4 we plan to ship a UI for key lifecycle management (rotate, revoke, audit who rotated) and an audit view tied to rotation events. ETA: internal beta in ~10 weeks.

Alex (Eng): Great. Another question from the customer: Does SOC 2 scope cover Private deployments? They want to include a Private VPC deployment in the attestation.

Maria (Security): Short version: our SOC 2 report covers Redwood control plane and hosted infra/services. For Private deployments it's a shared-responsibility model — Redwood provides control-plane controls and the customer controls infra. We provide a "SOC2 mapping" package (evidence templates + control mappings) to help customers and auditors. For fully air-gapped on-prem we can provide a tailored attestation letter and run readiness assessments but not extend our hosted SOC2 to their on-prem machines without an audit engagement.

Emily (Privacy): If they need ISO 27001 in addition, we can map our artifacts to ISO controls. For any control that lands on the customer (network, physical access), we call that out. It usually requires a short audit to get cert for a combined scope.

Sam (SRE): Practical item: if you enable long-term retention in Private and export to customer S3, decide whether retention lifecycle is managed by us (server-side) or by customer bucket lifecycle. Both patterns are supported; if the customer wants legal hold we recommend customer-side lifecycle so they manage deletions.

Alex (Eng): Is there a quick CLI snippet for enabling export to customer S3?

Maria (Security): Example for enabling S3 export via CLI (Private deployment):
```
redwoodctl export enable --deployment-id dp-12345 --export-target s3://acme-audit-logs --format json --encrypt --kms-key arn:aws:kms:...
```
(we'll add full flags to docs). Note: ensure your VPC peering and S3 endpoint are set up first.

Jordan (Product): Also note: we plan an audit-log-shipper sidecar for Private so you don't need to run fluentd yourself; that's roadmap item for next quarter.

Alex (Eng): Back to KMS/HSM — how do we handle key rotation notifications? Customer wants proof that rotation happened and who rotated.

Maria (Security): Rotation events are recorded in the audit log (who/when/operation). With BYOK we also record key reference changes. For higher assurance we can store signed rotation events in the evidence store and include them in the mapping package for auditors.

Emily (Privacy): Action for legal/compliance: we should add a short DSAR note for archived logs (how to search/delete items in long-retention buckets) — I'll draft it.

Sam (SRE): Action items: @Maria will post the audit-log export FAQ and the S3/syslog how-to. @Jordan will add BYOK/HSM diagrams and UI timeline to the roadmap page. @Emily will draft the DSAR guidance to attach to retention docs. I'll open an ops ticket to estimate storage costs for multi-year retention in Private.

ops-bot: Ticket created: #TICKET-4123 "audit-log-export-docs" assigned to Maria (Security) due 2025-01-15.

Maria (Security): Thanks — I'll queue the docs for review and @Sam please share storage estimates when ready. If anyone wants to pair on the design review for BYOK/HSM, ping me and we'll set up a sync. :thumbsup:
